title: 1954 AHSME Problem 22
statement: The expression \(\dfrac{2x^2-x}{(x+1)(x-2)}\) \({}-\dfrac{4+x}{(x+1)(x-2)}\) cannot be evaluated for \(x=-1\) or \(x=2,\) since division by zero is not allowed. For other values of \(x:\)

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: The expression takes on many different values.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: The expression has only the value \(2.\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: The expression has only the value \(1.\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
The expression always has a value between \(-1\) and
\(2.\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
The expression has a value greater than \(2\) or less than
\(-1.\)

solutions.text:
Combining the numerators gives \[ \begin{gathered} 2x^2-x-(4+x)\\ =2x^2-2x-4\\ =2(x+1)(x-2). \end{gathered} \] For the allowed values \(x\ne-1,2,\) the factors cancel and the expression equals \(2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Combine the two fractions over their common denominator
